title: Erasing one bit (Landauer's bound)

data.source: Overdamped Langevin particles in a double well U = x^4/4 - b x^2/2 - F x, flattened, tilted and restored over five durations; seeded

prediction: Work to erase one bit follows W = c + B/duration with c within 0.1 of ln 2 = 0.693 kT, never below that floor, and B at least 12 (friction times the squared distance the particles must be carried).
baseline: Landauer's bound kT ln 2, and the known finite-time law that the extra cost falls as 1/duration, with the same least value for B.
why: The floor and the cost of hurrying both came out as predicted. But R6 is, in its own words, existing thermodynamic-length mathematics, and the owner's energy claim for one bit is Landauer's bound renamed. Nothing new is predicted.
